name: CT-RATE
description: CT-RATE is a public dataset that pairs 3D medical images with corresponding textual reports. It comprises 25,692 non-contrast 3D chest CT scans from 21,304 unique patients, totaling 50,188 reconstructed CT volumes (over 14.3 million 2D slices). Each scan is accompanied by its corresponding radiology report including impression and findings sections. Each volume is also annotated with 18 abnormalities. The dataset is used to develop CT-CLIP, a CT-focused contrastive language-image pretraining framework, and CT-CHAT, a vision-language foundational chat model for 3D chest CT volumes.
creator: Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci, Sezgin Er, Bjoern Menze, and collaborators from University of Zurich, ETH Zurich, Istanbul Medipol University, Boston University, NIH, Imperial College London, University Hospital Zurich, FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg
publisher: Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital / University of Zurich
citeAs: Hamamci, I.E., Er, S., Wang, C., et al. Generalist foundation models from a multimodal dataset for 3D computed tomography. arXiv:2403.17834v5 [cs.CV] 8 Feb 2026.
rai:dataCollection: CT-RATE was curated from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital, consisting of non-contrast chest CT volumes acquired between May 2015 and January 2023. The dataset includes 50,188 reconstructed CT volumes from 25,692 distinct CT experiments conducted on 21,304 unique patients. CT volumes are reconstructed using various techniques for different window settings. Each CT exam is accompanied by a radiology report authored by a radiologist, including impression and findings sections. Reports were originally in Turkish and translated to English using the Google Translate API, reviewed and corrected by bilingual final-year medical students. All patient data was anonymized before computational analysis.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Detailed metadata for the second external validation set (UPMC) is not publicly available, as it is a private dataset and cannot be shared. The RAD-ChestCT external validation set lacks a Mosaic attenuation label and text reports, limiting certain evaluations.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Non-contrast chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology text reports from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital, acquired between May 2015 and January 2023. CT volumes were acquired using Philips (61.5%), Siemens (30.1%), and PNMS (8.4%) CT scanners. Volumes are provided in resolutions of 512×512 px (65.4%), 768×768 px (4.2%), and 1024×1024 px (30.4%). Radiology reports are structured into four sections: clinical information, technique, findings, and impression, originally authored in Turkish by radiologists.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Reports were anonymized by removing all personal information using regular expressions to identify and eliminate date-related information and patient-doctor identifiers. Anonymized reports were translated from Turkish to English using the Google Translate API. Bilingual final-year medical students reviewed and corrected all translations and removed any residual personal information. For CT volumes, identifying information about patients and medical professionals was removed from metadata. Volumes involving contrast material or body parts other than the chest were excluded. Each chest CT volume's orientation was standardized by examining its metadata.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Each CT volume was resized to achieve uniform spacing of 0.75 mm in the x-axis and y-axis and 1.5 mm in the z-axis. CT volumes were then either center-cropped or padded to reach a consistent resolution of 480×480×240. Each CT volume was converted to Hounsfield Unit (HU) values using intercept and slope values from the metadata. HU values were clipped to a range of -1000 to 1000. During training, values were normalized to a range of -1 to 1. The dataset was divided into training (20,000 patients) and internal validation (1,304 patients) sets.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Multi-abnormality labels were extracted from radiology reports using an automated text classifier. A pretrained language model, RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m, was finetuned on 1,000 manually annotated reports for 18 distinct abnormalities. Annotations were created by merging findings and impression sections. Conditions not referenced in either section were considered absent. Similar conditions were grouped (e.g., left and right mucoid impactions under mucoid impaction; lung opacity, density increase, and ground-glass opacities under lung opacity; lung and fissural nodules as lung nodules). The annotated reports were divided into training (80%, 800 reports) and validation (20%, 200 reports) sets. The finetuned model was then applied to classify the remaining 24,692 reports. Additionally, organ-level anatomical segmentation labels were generated using a state-of-the-art segmentation model (CADS). For expert evaluation of CT-CHAT report generation, three board-certified radiologists independently rated 150 reports per model on a 0-10 scale based on predefined clinical criteria covering finding description, localisation, terminology, and overall clinical adequacy.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The finetuned text encoder's performance in automatic label extraction was evaluated using precision, recall, and F1 scores for each of the 18 abnormalities, showing robust classification (F1 scores ranging from 0.95 to 1.00 across abnormalities). For expert radiologist evaluation of CT-CHAT, cases were stratified by Llama score into low (0-3), medium (4-6), and high (7-10) clinical accuracy ranges, with 50 cases selected from each range to ensure balanced difficulty. Three board-certified radiologists independently scored reports, and results were presented as mean scores and violin plots.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The CT-RATE dataset is publicly accessible via HuggingFace (https://huggingface.co/datasets/ibrahimhamamci/CT-RATE). The authors plan to extend CT-RATE with multi-abnormality segmentation and localization labels for 3D chest CT volumes as future work. Organ-level anatomical segmentation labels are already openly available through the CT-RATE repository on Hugging Face. Trained models and codebase are publicly available at https://github.com/ibrahimethemhamamci/CT-CLIP and https://github.com/ibrahimethemhamamci/CT-CHAT.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Patient age (ranging from 18 to 102 years, mean 48.8 years), sex (41.6% female, 58.4% male), and medical history are included in the dataset metadata. All personal information pertaining to patients and medical professionals was anonymized before release. CT volumes, associated metadata, and radiology text reports were anonymized prior to any computational analysis.
rai:dataSocialImpact: CT-RATE addresses critical challenges in 3D medical imaging by providing the first large-scale open-source dataset pairing 3D chest CT volumes with radiology reports. This enables development of AI models that can assist radiologists in identifying pathologies, reducing workload, and potentially saving lives in situations where immediate radiological expertise is not available. The dataset and associated models lay the groundwork for future innovations in medical AI and improved patient care. A user-friendly graphical interface is provided to allow non-experts to interact with CT-CHAT, broadening accessibility for educational and clinical research settings.
rai:dataBiases: CT-RATE is a single-center dataset from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital in Türkiye, which may introduce biases related to a single geographic and clinical setting, potentially limiting generalizability to other populations. The dataset reflects real-world heterogeneity in CT scanners, acquisition protocols, and reconstruction techniques. CT-CLIP depends on the specific terminology used in reports and the choice of prompts during zero-shot detection, and variability in how diseases are described across radiology reports can affect detection accuracy. Performance increases with larger training sets, suggesting that incorporating data from multiple institutions and more diverse patient populations could further enhance model robustness.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset originates from a single institution (single-center), which may limit generalizability to other populations and geographic regions. Current models are limited to chest CT volumes and do not cover other 3D imaging modalities such as MRI and PET scans, or other anatomical regions. CT-CLIP depends on specific terminology in reports and prompt engineering for zero-shot detection. The quality of CT-CHAT generated reports remains insufficient for clinical deployment. The absence of true 3D VQA benchmarks limits comparative evaluation. Detailed metadata for the UPMC external validation set is not publicly available.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation, and Testing of AI models for: (1) multi-abnormality detection in 3D chest CT volumes, (2) CT volume retrieval (volume-to-volume and report-to-volume), (3) radiology report generation, (4) visual question answering for 3D chest CT, (5) contrastive language-image pretraining for 3D medical imaging, (6) fine-tuning vision-language models for medical imaging tasks. The dataset supports zero-shot classification, supervised classification, and fine-tuning approaches. Not recommended for clinical deployment without further validation, as models have not yet met clinical deployment thresholds.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each CT volume is annotated with 18 abnormality labels extracted automatically from radiology reports. For expert radiologist evaluation, 150 reports per model were rated by 3 board-certified radiologists.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Three board-certified radiologists performed expert evaluation: two board-certified thoracic radiologists from Zurich (R1, R2) and one from Istanbul (R3). Manual annotation of 1,000 reports for finetuning the automated label extractor was performed by the research team (specific demographics not detailed). Translation review was performed by bilingual final-year medical students.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m (finetuned for automated abnormality label extraction from radiology reports), Google Translate API (for Turkish to English translation of radiology reports), Llama 3.1 8B (for generating VQA question-answer pairs), Llama 3.1 70B (for clinical accuracy evaluation of model outputs), TotalSegmentator (for organ-level anatomical segmentation labels and pulmonary nodule segmentation), CADS - Comprehensive Anatomical Dataset and Segmentation model (for anatomical segmentation labels)
